meta.name: Status Epilepticus — Post-Ictal Airway Failure Requiring RSI

patient.name: Gregory Aldana
patient.chiefComplaint: Found seizing at home, now post-ictal with noisy breathing

history.hpi: Wife called 911 after finding the patient having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in the living room. She reports the seizure had already been going on for several minutes before she called, and by the time crews arrive convulsive movement has stopped, but the patient remains unresponsive with loud snoring respirations. No known trigger reported.
history.events: Wife heard a crash, found patient convulsing on the living room floor, called 911 immediately

scene.location: Single-family home, living room, patient supine on the floor near an overturned side table
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; wife present and cooperative
scene.bystanders: Wife present, witnessed the seizure, reports it lasted at least 6-7 minutes before EMS arrival
visualCues: Patient supine, unresponsive, not currently convulsing
Loud snoring (stertorous) respirations audible from the doorway
Overturned side table and lamp near patient

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 51-year-old male down on the living room floor, unresponsive, with loud snoring respirations. Wife reports witnessed generalized convulsions lasting over 6 minutes that have just stopped.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Partially obstructed, loud snoring respirations, tongue falling posterior
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong, skin diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: No purposeful movement, occasional myoclonic twitch of the left hand

transitions.condition: Crew opens the airway with positioning/jaw thrust, places an NPA, applies oxygen, and checks blood glucose per the seizure protocol's actively-seizing/post-ictal workup.

phases.name: Airway repositioned and glucose checked
phases.description: Crew repositions the airway, inserts a nasopharyngeal airway, applies oxygen, and checks blood glucose, which returns normal. Respirations and SpO2 improve somewhat but the patient remains GCS 5 with persistent snoring despite the adjunct.
phases.triggerCondition: After basic airway maneuvers and NPA placement fail to fully resolve the snoring, and glucometry returns normal, ruling out hypoglycemia as the cause of ongoing altered mental status.

clinicalPresentation.airway: NPA in place, snoring persists though somewhat improved
otherFindings: NPA in place, partial improvement in air movement
Blood glucose 118 mg/dL — hypoglycemia ruled out

expectedActions.shortAction: Reposition airway (chin-lift/jaw thrust); insert NPA given intact gag reflex
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If signs of airway obstruction are present and a chin-lift, jaw thrust, positioning, and/or suctioning does not alleviate it, place oropharyngeal airway (if gag reflex is absent) or nasopharyngeal airway
expectedActions.rationale: The tongue and soft tissue are the source of the obstruction in a post-ictal patient; an NPA is appropriate given an intact gag reflex.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply oxygen and place pulse oximetry/waveform capnography to monitor ventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Place pulse oximeter and/or waveform capnography to monitor oxygenation/ventilation. Administer oxygen as appropriate with a target of achieving 94–98% saturation
expectedActions.rationale: Capnography and SpO2 guide the decision for airway escalation as the patient fails to improve.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose given ongoing altered mental status after seizure
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If still actively seizing, check blood glucose level. If less than 60 mg/dL, treat per the Hypoglycemia Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out hypoglycemia as a treatable cause of persistent AMS/seizure activity.

transitions.condition: Despite basic airway adjuncts, the patient remains GCS 5 with inadequate ventilation (RR 10, EtCO2 48, SpO2 91%) and cannot protect his airway; crew proceeds with RSI per the Airway Management guideline.
Crew continues basic airway maneuvers alone without escalating to RSI despite persistent hypoventilation and hypoxia.

phases.name: RSI performed for airway failure
phases.description: Crew recognizes ongoing airway failure despite basic adjuncts and proceeds with rapid sequence intubation: preoxygenation, premedication, induction with etomidate, paralysis with rocuronium, and successful tube placement confirmed with waveform capnography.
phases.triggerCondition: The patient remains unable to protect his airway with persistent hypoventilation and borderline oxygenation despite NPA and oxygen; two experienced airway practitioners proceed with RSI per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube, confirmed placement
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mechanically ventilated, bilateral breath sounds equal
otherFindings: Waveform capnography confirms placement, EtCO2 trending toward normal

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure ventilation for at least 2 minutes before RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate preoxygenation extends the safe apnea window during intubation attempts.

expectedActions.shortAction: Etomidate 22.5 mg IV push (90 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 22.5 mg) for induction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Etomidate provides rapid induction with minimal hemodynamic effect for RSI.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 90 mg IV push (90 kg × 1 mg/kg = 90 mg) for paralysis
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Full paralysis optimizes first-pass intubation success and reduces trauma from resistance.

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm ETT placement with waveform capnography, breath sounds, and absent gastric sounds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and prevents an unrecognized esophageal intubation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 90-180 mcg IV (90 kg × 1-2 mcg/kg) plus midazolam for post-intubation sedation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Intubated patients should be provided appropriate sedation with sedative or opioid medications... Fentanyl 1-2 mcg/kg And Midazolam 0.02 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing sedation prevents awareness and agitation against the tube after paralytic wears off.

transitions.condition: ETT is secured, mechanically ventilated with EtCO2 35-45 target, and patient is packaged for transport with continuous monitoring.

phases.name: Tube secured and ventilation optimized
phases.description: Patient is intubated, sedated, mechanically ventilated with EtCO2 maintained 35-45 mmHg, and transported with continuous waveform capnography and reassessment for tube displacement.
phases.triggerCondition: After successful RSI and tube confirmation, the patient is secured, sedated, and prepared for transport with ongoing capnography monitoring.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mechanically ventilated, equal bilateral breath sounds
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, skin warm and pink
otherFindings: ETT depth unchanged, secured with commercial holder

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously monitor waveform capnography during transport, reassessing after each patient movement
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Continuously monitor correct airway placement with waveform capnography during treatment and transport, paying particular attention to reassessing after each patient movement
expectedActions.rationale: Tube displacement is a leading cause of preventable deterioration after successful RSI.

phases.name: RSI delayed despite ongoing failure
phases.description: Crew continues basic airway maneuvers without escalating to RSI. The patient's ventilation continues to deteriorate, with rising EtCO2 and falling SpO2 indicating progression toward respiratory failure and hypoxic injury.
phases.triggerCondition: Basic airway adjuncts alone are continued despite persistent hypoventilation, and the crew does not escalate to RSI as the patient's respiratory status worsens.

clinicalPresentation.airway: NPA in place, worsening obstruction, snoring louder
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak, skin cyanotic at lips
otherFindings: EtCO2 climbing, SpO2 falling despite oxygen

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize impending respiratory failure and escalate to BVM/RSI without further delay
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Many airway/breathing issues in seizing patients can be managed without intubation or placement of an advanced airway. Reserve these measures for patients that fail less invasive maneuvers as noted above
expectedActions.rationale: Bradycardia and rising EtCO2 with falling SpO2 signal hypoxia-driven decompensation requiring immediate escalation.
